To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a nanomolar concentration of drag-reducing polymers can dramatically inhibit experimental metastasis of breast tumor cells in mice by preventing cancer cells from extravading into the lung.
a blood-soluble non-toxic drag-reducing chemical agent can inhibit metastasis by preventing tumor cell extravasation.
blood-soluble, non-toxic, non-immunosuppressive drag-reducing polymers, when administered at very low concentrations (nanomolar), inhibit experimental metastasis of tumor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new direction of cancer research that is focused on the physical and rheological aspects of the tumor microenvironment and the blood flow in the vicinity of the blood vessels.

a novel concept that the rheological characteristics of blood flow can be modified by blood-soluble chemicals to inhibit extravasation of cancer and other cells and subsequent development and growth of metastases.
the fundamental understanding of the role of blood flow in cancer metastasis and with the development of a new approach to cancer metastasis prevention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a proof-of-principle demonstration that the physical approach of blood flow modification can be effective in preventing metastasis.

the results of the present study provide the first proof-of-concept that a physical/rheological approach to prevent cancer cells extravasation and metastasis is feasible and that this approach is worthy of further investigations.
the present study demonstrated that a nanomolar concentration of a drag-reducing blood-soluble polymer can prevent metastasis of human cancer cells in a mouse model of cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a nanomolar concentration of non-toxic blood soluble drag-reducing polymers can be used to inhibit metastasis of human cancer cells.
we have discovered a new paradigm in cancer therapy, i.e. physical, as opposed to traditional chemical, approach to prevent metastasis.
the blood-soluble drug-reducing polymer is a promising candidate for a new class of anti-metastatic agent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a physical intervention to the blood flow can prevent cancer cells from metastasis.
a novel approach of using blood-soluble agents to prevent metastasis by modifying blood flow in the tumor microenvironment may be a promising new direction in the field.
the physical/rheological approach can be used as a new paradigm in anti-cancer therapy.
